database_meta.title: Avasta World Database - Entangled and the Founding of Malmskor
database_meta.purpose: Lookup table for adding and retrieving Avasta world information. Rebuilt from the Chronicles Log (Cycles 1-124) using the earlier world_database.md as the structural template, then extended with characters, creatures, items, materials, processes, blueprints, failed attempts, ID tables, a timeline and continuity flags. Every named element carries an image_prompt.

current_state.situation_summary: Entangled and the crew (Dede, Helrune, Roseblossom) hold Malmskor, a windmill-powered forge-fortress on a 50 m ledge of Lone Mountain. Steel has been smelted once (Cycles 101-102). The defence tower is shoulder height with no dome and the heavy crossbow has no bow stave (prod). A second charcoal clamp is smouldering on the ledge and unfired clay crucibles are drying for the next smelt. A ginger-furred catfolk hunter looking for Ryu is sheltering in the outer foyer until dawn.

conventions.hallucination_flag: true marks something that entered the narrative without being logically earned (spontaneous manifestation, retroactive inventory, regression or amnesia, degradation). Kept so later cycles can correct or retcon it. hallucination_reason explains why.
conventions.image_prompt: Self-contained visual description of the element. Prepend image_style_guide.global_style_prefix when generating images so everything stays visually consistent.
conventions.pegboard_id: Code the player defined in the in-world ID lookup table (see id_lookup_table). Entries without one have no player-defined code.
conventions.numbers: Quantities (kg, metres, temperatures) are copied from the chronicle text. Where the chronicle gives no figure none is invented.

image_style_guide.global_style_prefix: Gritty dark-fantasy survival concept art, highly detailed, cold desaturated palette of slate grey, frost white and iron rust with warm orange firelight accents, hard winter light, practical hand-forged and dry-stacked craftsmanship, visible wear, frost and soot
image_style_guide.lighting_notes: Outdoors: overcast or low winter sun, blowing frost, long shadows. Indoors: warm furnace glow and charcoal embers against cold grey stone.
image_style_guide.material_palette: Grey shale, slate, milky quartz, rust-red hematite, pale bauxite, black basalt, dark charcoal, tan goat hide, raw conifer timber, hand-forged dark iron.
image_style_guide.negative_prompt_suggestions: modern materials, plastic, neon colours, clean pristine surfaces, cartoon style, guns, text or watermarks, gemstone magic glow (magic has not been established in this world)
image_style_guide.consistency_notes: No facial, hair or skin descriptions of the four crew exist in the chronicle. Pick them once and reuse the same wording in every later prompt.

world.world_description: A living, shared AI-generated MMO sandbox world of brutal sub-zero wilderness: windswept southern coastal cliffs, hidden sea caves, tidal gullies, a reed-choked alluvial floodplain, snowy alpine conifer slopes and a lone mountain riddled with iron, bauxite, quartz, copper and lead-silver veins. Survival, mining, smithing and settlement building drive the story. The current focus is the dwarf Entangled and the mountain stronghold Malmskor (Iron Ledge).
world.image_prompt: Sweeping view of a frozen fantasy wilderness: grey coastal cliffs and crashing sea in the south, a reed-filled river floodplain, and a lone jagged mountain rising in the north-east with a tiny fortified stone ledge and a spinning windmill clinging to its southern face, under a pale overcast sky.

world_rules.magic: No functioning magic has been demonstrated. Rune etching (Cycles 3, 8, 12, 28, 31, 33) and the rune-awakening dream (Cycle 112) all failed to produce any energy, glow or effect. Runes are currently decorative or symbolic only.
world_rules.technology_tier: Stone age through bloomery iron and steel, with wind-powered mechanics (cam, lantern gear, winch, bellows, trip-hammer). Not yet available: blast furnace, cast iron, wire drawing, glass or mirrors, paper, rubber, salt, lime, springs of spring steel, rolling mills, rotary drills.
world_rules.realism_rule: When a prompt asks for something the world cannot yet support, the narrative substitutes what can be done and logs the blocker (see failed_or_blocked_attempts).
world_rules.survival: Cold is the constant threat. Wet skin freezes on the ledge, clay and mud flash-freeze, food spoils slowly in the permafrost freezer, water comes from melted ice and basin rainwater.
world_rules.social: Visitors are treated as friendly by default; the crew arms up first when a threat is unknown. Crew members follow Entangled's assigned daily tasks and give honest engineering pushback.

calendar.approximate_clock: Pre-dawn around 05:00-06:00, Morning to about 10:00, Noon around midday, Afternoon to about 18:00, Evening to about 22:00, Midnight covers the deep night to about 02:00.
calendar.numbering_rule: Cycle 1 was Noon on 2026-10-06. Cycles 1-4 (Noon, Afternoon, Evening, Midnight) fall on Oct 6. From Cycle 5 (Pre-dawn, Oct 7) each day holds six cycles, and a Midnight cycle belongs to the date of the evening before it. Date for cycle n (n>=5) = Oct 7 plus floor((n-5)/6) days.

global_weather.baseline_climate: Sub-zero arctic/alpine conditions with frequent gale-force winds, blizzards and nights of -10C to -20C. Brief midday or afternoon thaws push the air just above freezing and turn scree and clay to slick mud.

notable_weather_events.event: Biting sub-zero coastal gale on arrival.
Mid-morning thaw melted the frozen clay render off the shelter wall.
Night freeze made the cliff face contract with loud cracks and scree slides.
About -20C at nightfall; ledge dead and locked in ice.
-12C with violent gusts; summit scouting cancelled.
-10C gale during the first elevator test.
Blazing sun and fast thaw, scree turned to mud.
Highland chill and howling wind at midnight.

global_weather.image_prompt: Violent grey alpine weather over a cliff ledge: horizontal wind-blown sleet and rime frost, shredded cloud, frozen puddles and a thin low sun breaking through.

total_population.notes: Crew: Entangled, Dede, Helrune, Roseblossom. Hostile: masked elf raider (fled east, Cycle 48). Visitor: unnamed ginger catfolk hunter (arrived Cycle 124). Ryu and Cisero are reported by Entangled as having built a timber hall at Ironhold and then marched south.

regions.name: Southern Coastal Cliffs and Crags
regions.description: Windswept southern coast of shale, flint and quartz with sub-zero gales, eroding gullies, tidal shallows and a conifer wood edge to the north. Entangled's arrival point and first home (Cycles 1-17).
regions.region_weather: Biting sub-zero coastal gales, blowing sleet and freezing ocean spray.
regions.image_prompt: Wild southern coastline of fractured grey shale cliffs and eroded gullies, sleet blowing off a churning black sea, quartz-veined rock and wind-bent dark conifers inland.

sub_regions.name: Southern Cliffs Ledge
sub_regions.image_prompt: A bare windswept cliff-top ridge of broken shale and flint nodules above a frozen gully, with a low dry-stone mound blending into the rock.

locations.name: Camouflaged Corbelled Stone Bunker
locations.description: Dry-stacked shale and flint corbelled half-dome without mortar that swallowed an old dry-stone windbreak. A tight horizontal viewing slit faces north and east. Flint chips wedged into the outer cracks make it look like a natural rock mound; it did not budge under a full-weight shoulder slam. Used for Cycles 1-3 as shelter, hearth and lookout.
locations.image_prompt: A camouflaged corbelled half-dome bunker of dry-stacked grey shale slabs and flint chips on a sleet-blown cliff ridge, one narrow horizontal viewing slit facing the sea, looking like a natural pile of broken rock.

facilities.name: Wired Wooden Horn and Microphone
facilities.description: A listening horn with a wire run, already present in the original dry-stone windbreak and checked by Entangled in Cycle 3.
facilities.hallucination_reason: Spontaneous Manifestation Hallucination: appeared in Cycle 1 to satisfy the prompt's request for a concealed lookout without any technological progression from raw stone.
facilities.image_prompt: A crude wooden horn with a thin wire running from it and a small microphone element, set in a dry-stone alcove inside a dark stone bunker.

facilities.name: Driftwood and Kelp Hearth
facilities.description: Flint-struck fire in shaved bark and dried salty kelp; smoke drafts out through the viewing slit. First cooked the predatory lizard meat (Cycle 2).
facilities.image_prompt: A small hearth of blackened stones inside a cramped stone dome, glowing driftwood and kelp embers, smoke curling toward a narrow slit.

facilities.name: Shale Slab Sleet Catcher
facilities.description: Wide dished shale slab set under the outside ledge to catch blowing sleet, brought inside to melt (Cycle 2).
facilities.image_prompt: A wide dished slab of grey shale wedged beneath a rock ledge, half full of frozen sleet and meltwater.

facilities.name: Etched Flint Rune Stone
facilities.description: Elongated flint stone with crisp angular runes scratched by a flint flake (Cycle 3). Inert; symbolic only.
facilities.image_prompt: An elongated grey flint stone scratched with crisp angular runic lines, lying on a rough stone floor in firelight.

sub_regions.name: Coastal Sea-Cave Drift Mine
sub_regions.image_prompt: A hidden sea cave mouth in a quartz-streaked cliff, tidal shallows in front and a pitch-dark chamber behind with frozen clay and frost.

locations.name: Concealed Sea Cave (Drift Mine)
locations.description: Natural quartz and shale sea cave with an excavated mound of frozen clay and a permafrost alcove. Wind drops instantly inside. Entangled mapped it onto a shale slab, laid a flint-and-quartz hearth ring, hung a shale-slab windbreak across the entrance (Cycle 12) and cracked into a hematite pocket in the rear wall (Cycle 14). Abandoned because it was too cold for dwarf blood.
locations.image_prompt: A cramped sea cave with quartz-veined walls, a half-height wall of stacked shale slabs across the entrance, a ring of flint and quartz stones with a small fire, and a frozen clay alcove at the back.

facilities.name: Pre-Excavated Drift Mine and Woven Fish Trap
facilities.description: An old excavated mound of frozen clay and a woven funnel fish trap found in the cave in Cycle 4. The trap never caught anything (Cycle 5) but held against the tide.
facilities.hallucination_reason: Spontaneous Manifestation Hallucination: appeared in Cycle 4 to bypass excavating a mine with a driftwood spear and to hand over an advanced food trap.
facilities.image_prompt: A woven reed funnel fish trap half-submerged in icy tidal shallows at the mouth of a dark sea cave, next to a heap of frozen grey clay.

facilities.name: Circular Flint-and-Quartz Hearth Ring
facilities.description: Loose flint and quartz stones arranged in a sturdy circle as the foundation for a furnace and hearth (Cycle 5). Fed with kelp and driftwood in Cycles 7, 14 and 16.
facilities.image_prompt: A neat circle of white quartz and dark flint stones on a cave floor holding glowing driftwood embers and white ash.

facilities.name: Shale Slab Cave Map
facilities.description: Cavern map scratched into a wide shale slab showing clay deposits, the frozen lizard-man corpse and the route to the entrance (Cycle 5).
facilities.image_prompt: A wide grey shale slab scratched with a simple cave map, lines and small markers, leaning against a cave wall.

facilities.name: Shale Ledger Slabs
facilities.description: Slabs used for rune-test notes (Cycle 12), inventory, stats and the periscope design (Cycle 13), and ore tallies (Cycle 14). Conclusion recorded: runes must be carved deeper.
facilities.image_prompt: A shale slab deeply scratched with columns of tally marks, tool sketches and a vertical shaft diagram with two cone mirrors.

facilities.name: Shale Slab Windbreak Door
facilities.description: Heavy shale slabs stacked across the lower half of the cave entrance to cut the wind (Cycle 12).
facilities.image_prompt: Heavy flat shale slabs stacked as a waist-high wall across a cave mouth, ocean spray and frost beyond.

facilities.name: Hematite Pocket
facilities.description: Iron-stained gravel and workable hematite nodules exposed by the quartz pickaxe in the rear wall (Cycle 14). First iron ore found in the world.
facilities.image_prompt: A cracked cave wall seam opening onto a pocket of rust-red hematite nodules and iron-stained gravel.

facilities.name: Frozen Lizard-Man Corpse
facilities.description: Icy corpse of a lizard-man frozen solid to the cave stone. Cause of death unknown.
facilities.image_prompt: A frost-covered scaly humanoid lizard corpse frozen to the floor of a dark sea cave, rime on its scales.

sub_regions.name: Northern Coastal Trail (Conifer Edge and River Trail)
sub_regions.image_prompt: A frozen trail along the edge of a dark conifer wood above a rocky river gully, an old timber road and bodies frozen to the rocks.

locations.name: Conifer Edge Timber Road
locations.description: Crude timber road laid over frozen mud at the edge of the conifer woods, splattered with old goat blood. Noted as a good hunting spot once the weather breaks.
locations.image_prompt: A crude road of laid logs over frozen mud at the edge of a dark conifer forest, dark old blood splashes on the timbers.

locations.name: Troll Kill Site (River Trail)
locations.description: Two massive troll bodies frozen to the rock. One was torn open; the other had a heavy iron bolt driven deep into its chest. Whoever did this has serious firepower. Entangled judged the area too hot to build a hidden home.
locations.image_prompt: Two enormous frozen troll bodies on icy riverside rocks, one torn open, the other with a thick iron bolt buried in its chest, frost on their grey hides.

sub_regions.name: Eastern Crags and Tidal Gully
sub_regions.image_prompt: Fractured grey bedrock crags with a green-stained quartz vein, a protected tidal gully and scattered goat tracks.

locations.name: Malachite-Crusted Quartz Vein
locations.description: Strange quartz vein crusted in vivid green malachite (copper). Bypassed because iron was the goal.
locations.image_prompt: A white quartz vein in dark bedrock crusted with vivid green malachite.

locations.name: Protected Tidal Gully Goat Ground
locations.description: Sheltered tidal gully with cloven tracks and droppings where Entangled speared the first feral goat from a ledge (Cycle 8).
locations.image_prompt: A narrow rocky tidal gully with frost on the scree and a small feral goat picking along the rocks below an overhang.

regions.name: River Marsh and Alluvial Floodplain
regions.description: Soggy alluvial floodplain between the coast and Lone Mountain: calf-deep pools, thick reeds, cycad and fern stands, wild rice, granite boulder fields and giant crocodilians. Crossed in Cycles 18-21.
regions.region_weather: Cold, damp inland air, above freezing during midday thaws, bitter at dusk.
regions.image_prompt: A grey winter floodplain of slow brown channels, tall dead reeds, cycads and ferns, with a lone mountain on the horizon and a giant crocodile sunk in a pool.

sub_regions.name: Alluvial Floodplain and River Branches
sub_regions.image_prompt: Flat marsh of sluggish pools, trampled reeds and wild rice patches split by a shallow bedrock river branch.

locations.name: Floodplain Crossing and Wooded Central Rise
locations.description: Calf-deep pools and clay flats crossed on foot, skirting deeper channels past a wooded central rise. Entangled stowed the crampons here so clay would not drag.
locations.image_prompt: A traveller wading calf-deep through a reedy marsh channel towards a small wooded rise, mud and ice on the reeds.

locations.name: Gravel Bar Lunch Camp
locations.description: Dry gravel bar behind a wall of cycads and ferns, away from the croc water. A smokeless reed-pith fire was lit here, goat meat eaten and the three-clawed gauntlet crafted. Fire smothered with river mud.
locations.image_prompt: A small dry gravel bar hidden behind cycads and ferns with a smokeless fire and a dwarf lashing claws onto a rawhide glove.

locations.name: Western River Branch Crossing
locations.description: Shallow western branch of the river with slick bedrock and wet cobbles, crossed using the iron crampons. Wild rice and trampled reeds on the far side.
locations.image_prompt: A shallow river branch over slick grey bedrock and wet cobbles with wild rice and trampled reeds on the bank.

locations.name: Northern Woods Edge and Reed Stands
locations.description: Last tall river reeds and the sparse edge of the northern woods. Dry reed stalks and deadwood were bundled for fuel. The bellowing crocodilians stay behind in the bottomlands.
locations.image_prompt: The ragged edge of a northern wood at dusk, tall dry reed stands in the foreground, a mountain slope rising behind.

sub_regions.name: Granite Ridge Overhang and Limonite Outcrop
sub_regions.image_prompt: Rising ground of broken granite and boulder fields with a rust-red vein cutting through the stone.

locations.name: Raptor Carcass Overhang
locations.description: Overhang sheltering the picked-clean carcass of a feathered predator. Four large curved foot claws and several tough hide strips were salvaged in about half an hour.
locations.image_prompt: A picked-clean skeleton of a large feathered predator under a granite overhang, huge curved foot claws still attached.

locations.name: Low-Grade Limonite Outcrop
locations.description: Rust-red limonite vein through north-east rocks. Three fist-sized chunks were struck; two kept, one discarded to save weight.
locations.image_prompt: A rust-orange limonite vein running through grey granite, fresh chip marks from a pickaxe.

anomalous_items.hallucination_reason: Retroactive Inventory Manifestation Hallucination: introduced in Cycle 19 without ever being crafted, to logically explain how Entangled had crossed icy ground and cliffs in earlier cycles.
anomalous_items.image_prompt: A pair of rough hand-forged scrap-iron ice crampons with sharp spikes strapped over worn hide boots.

regions.name: Lone Mountain
regions.description: Isolated peak rising north-east of the marshes. Features a steep 50 m southern scree gully, an eastern ice-pool fault, a summit nobody has reached and deep seams of hematite, bauxite, quartz, copper and lead-silver. Home of Malmskor.
regions.region_weather: Extreme alpine freeze (-10C to -20C at night), violent vertical cliff updrafts and gales, daytime thaws that melt frost into mud.

temporary_visitors: Unnamed ginger catfolk hunter (outer foyer, from Cycle 124)

regions.image_prompt: A lone jagged mountain of grey rock and white quartz bands standing above a frozen basin, a tiny stone ledge with a spinning windmill and an elevator cabin hanging halfway up its southern face.

sub_regions.name: Southern Zigzag Gully and Conifer Slopes
sub_regions.image_prompt: A steep zigzag scree gully glazed in frost and black ice with carved footholds, descending 50 metres to scrubby conifer slopes.

locations.name: Southern Zigzag Gully
locations.description: Steep 50 m scree gully from the foot of the mountain up to the ledge. Chipped flat footholds (Cycle 24) and a wider smoothed sled trail (Cycle 29) make it passable; frozen it is treacherous without crampons. Largely replaced by the elevator since Cycle 86.
locations.image_prompt: A zigzagging frozen scree gully with chipped flat footholds and a smoothed haul trail, a rope hanging down a sheer cliff beside it.

locations.name: Lower Slope Iron-Bearing Vein
locations.description: Exposed vein of iron-bearing rock at the foot of the mountain. Yields: about 14 kg (Cycle 27), 25 kg on the sled (Cycle 30), about 8 kg of hematite (Cycle 43).
locations.image_prompt: A rust-red iron-bearing rock seam at the foot of a mountain with a wooden drag sled loaded with ore beside it.

locations.name: Lower Conifer and Scrub Line
locations.description: Low conifers, hardwood scrub and tough grasses at the western foot and lower slopes. Source of logs (three ~40 kg trunks in Cycle 79), branches, timber for beams and softwood for charcoal.
locations.image_prompt: A sparse line of low frost-bitten conifers and scrub at the foot of a mountain with fresh axe-cut stumps.

locations.name: Lower Southern Slopes Hunting Ground
locations.description: Goat grazing near an exposed quartz vein (Cycle 31) and a seasonal pool (Cycle 121). Goats and rock hyraxes hunted here.
locations.image_prompt: Rocky lower slopes with a pale quartz vein, a small seasonal pool and a feral goat grazing among frozen grass.

locations.name: Charcoal Survey Marker Line
locations.description: Bold charcoal survey lines struck on rock faces at regular spacing within line of sight (Cycle 92).
locations.image_prompt: Bold black charcoal lines and arrows drawn on pale rock faces at intervals across a frosty slope.

sub_regions.name: Eastern Ledge Fault and Frozen Mountain Pool
sub_regions.description: Deep rock fracture 40 m east of the ledge, reached by roping along the cliff, containing a freshwater pool frozen under 20 cm of ice, bordered by bauxite and quartz seams.
sub_regions.image_prompt: A deep rock crack on a cliff face holding a frozen pool under a thick ice sheet, white quartz and pale bauxite seams on its walls.

locations.name: Eastern Frozen Pool
locations.description: Source of 18 kg of clean ice slabs (Cycle 90), plus 12 kg of bauxite and 4 kg of quartz, then 15 kg more quartz and bauxite (Cycle 91). A clay-pipe water line to Malmskor failed because clay flash-froze (Cycle 91). Beneath it Entangled started an interior tunnel (Cycle 117).
locations.image_prompt: A frozen pool under a thick sheet of grey-blue ice in a narrow cliff fracture, two figures roped to the rock chopping ice with picks.

sub_regions.name: Lone Mountain Summit
sub_regions.description: Unexplored. Roseblossom was to search for a large body of water on the top (Cycle 81) but the climb was cancelled for a storm.
sub_regions.image_prompt: A storm-scoured bare mountain summit of ice-crusted rock under racing cloud, no signs of life.

locations.name: Summit Plateau (Unexplored)
locations.description: No scouting yet. Goals recorded: find a large body of water; use the summit for a panoramic view.
locations.image_prompt: A wind-swept snowy summit plateau with scattered boulders and a faint frozen tarn in the distance.

sub_regions.name: 50-Meter Southern Ledge (Malmskor / Iron Ledge)
sub_regions.description: Active mountain stronghold, forge workshop and deep mining adit. Entangled found a ready-made bloomery camp on the ledge in Cycle 22 and made it home; crew arrived Cycle 53; named Malmskor ('Iron Ledge') in Cycle 85. Some prompts type it 'Melmskor'.
sub_regions.image_prompt: A fortified stone ledge halfway up a sheer mountain face: a slanted shale-roofed foyer, a squat round stone tower, a four-sailed hide windmill spinning on the cliff and a timber elevator cabin hanging on a rope, frost and smoke in the air.

defenses_and_exterior.name: Original Bloomery Ledge Camp
defenses_and_exterior.description: Camp found on arrival: low windbreak walls dry-stacked from dense bauxite and ironstone around the rough cylindrical chimney of a smelting bloomery. Became the core of the shelter.
defenses_and_exterior.hallucination_reason: Spontaneous Manifestation Hallucination: a pre-built camp and bloomery appeared in Cycle 22 so the settlement could start without any construction.
defenses_and_exterior.image_prompt: A mountain ledge at night with low walls of rust-brown ironstone and pale bauxite around a stubby cylindrical clay bloomery chimney.

defenses_and_exterior.name: Slanted-Roof Stone Foyer and Ledge Barricade
defenses_and_exterior.description: Wide curving arc of dry-stacked quartz and bauxite boulders spanned with conifer logs and steep shale roof slabs to deflect rockslides. Rebuilt in Cycle 109 so the elevator winch, transfer shaft and elevator landing are inside it while the windmill sails stay clear. Sealed with clay-bauxite-quartz mud mortar (Cycle 111). The ledge's outer room: the catfolk visitor shelters here from Cycle 124.
defenses_and_exterior.image_prompt: A low curved dry-stacked boulder foyer with a steep slanted roof of grey shale slabs on conifer logs, clay-sealed seams, a timber elevator cabin open inside, frost on the roof.

defenses_and_exterior.name: Two-Level Circular Defense Tower and Gimbal Crossbow Turret
defenses_and_exterior.description: Circular dry-stacked bauxite and quartz wall at shoulder height (Cycle 115) with interior clay render (Cycle 121). Design: lower level gives secure access to the settlement, narrow steps curve up the inner wall to the upper level where the heavy crossbow sits on a central pivot pin in a lubricated socket with a U-bracket for tilt, under a dome with a panoramic window and stove-heat vents. Not yet built: dome and roof, upper deck, steps, window, vents, crossbow prod, net launcher.
defenses_and_exterior.image_prompt: A squat round shoulder-high dry-stone tower on a cliff ledge, interior walls smeared with grey clay, a timber crossbow frame leaning inside waiting for its dome.

defenses_and_exterior.name: Heavy Gimbal Crossbow (Incomplete)
defenses_and_exterior.description: Carved conifer tiller stock (Cycles 113-114) with forged rolling nut, sear lever and iron U-bracket. Heavy wooden bolts shaved from pine. Missing the prod (bow stave); the narrative admitted this in Cycle 116. Not yet mounted or fired.
defenses_and_exterior.image_prompt: A massive wooden crossbow tiller with a hand-forged iron rolling nut and trigger lever and a forged iron U-bracket, no bow limbs yet, beside a bundle of long wooden bolts.

defenses_and_exterior.name: Clay-Glazed Lead-Silver-Copper Rainwater Catchment Basin
defenses_and_exterior.description: Wide heavy alloy basin dished under the windmill-driven trip-hammer from lead-silver and copper matte, lined with river-clay mud-slip to stop lead leaching (Cycle 117). Water drawn from it was crisp and tasted clean (Cycle 119).
defenses_and_exterior.image_prompt: A wide dark metal basin on a stone ledge lined with smooth grey clay, filled with clear water, frost around the rim.

defenses_and_exterior.name: Ledge Turf-and-Dirt Charcoal Clamps
defenses_and_exterior.description: Conifer softwood and scrub boughs stacked around a central flue, buried under turf, dirt and crushed shale and left to smoulder. First clamp built Cycle 98, opened Cycle 101 for the steel smelt. Second built Cycle 122.
defenses_and_exterior.hallucination_reason: Facility Amnesia and Technological Regression Hallucination: the indoor entrance-wall charcoal kilns (W3, Cycle 54) were forgotten and the open-air dirt clamp used instead from Cycle 98.
defenses_and_exterior.image_prompt: A low earth-covered mound on a cliff ledge with a thin thread of smoke rising from the flue hole, conifer branch ends poking out of the turf.

defenses_and_exterior.name: Boulder Barricade and Entrance Chokepoint
defenses_and_exterior.description: Dede stacked massive basalt and ironstone boulders along the stone wall to choke the ledge entrance into a bottleneck.
defenses_and_exterior.image_prompt: Massive dark basalt and rusty ironstone boulders stacked along a narrow cliff ledge, leaving a tight gap to the stone doorway.

defenses_and_exterior.name: Slate Warning Sign
defenses_and_exterior.description: Slate slab chiselled WARNING! ENTANGLED PATH AHEAD, propped at the ledge. The original order was to place it at the start of the path below.
defenses_and_exterior.image_prompt: A slab of dark slate propped upright on a frosty ledge with deep chiselled capital letters reading WARNING! ENTANGLED PATH AHEAD.

defenses_and_exterior.name: Cliff-Rim Anchoring Notch
defenses_and_exterior.description: Deep V-notch chiselled into a solid dark rock vein at the cliff rim to seat the main winch axle.
defenses_and_exterior.image_prompt: A deep V-shaped notch chiselled into the dark rock lip of a cliff edge, rope fibre and frost around it.

defenses_and_exterior.name: 85 cm Cliff Vent Shaft
defenses_and_exterior.description: Horizontal vent bored into the cliff face (40, then 65, then 85 cm deep). Later the base of the layered chimney of the quartz-bauxite furnace (Cycle 72).
defenses_and_exterior.image_prompt: A neat round vent shaft bored into a rock face beside a cliff ledge, soot staining the lip.

defenses_and_exterior.name: Hide Drying Rack
defenses_and_exterior.description: Wooden rack on the ledge where the young goat hide is stretched tight to dry in the mountain breeze.
defenses_and_exterior.image_prompt: A simple wooden rack on a cliff ledge with a stretched goat hide drying in the wind.

defenses_and_exterior.name: Seamless Conifer Plank Door with Tumbler Lock
defenses_and_exterior.description: Seamless door of hewn conifer planks pegged and lashed together (Cycle 37). Lock: dwarf-forged iron-and-copper tumbler lock with sliding tumblers, latch and casing, forged Cycle 61 and engaged from Cycle 62. Tested smooth in Cycle 124.
defenses_and_exterior.image_prompt: A heavy seamless door of pale hewn conifer planks pegged together set in a clay-sealed stone wall with a dark iron-and-copper tumbler lock plate.

transport_and_power.name: Windmill-Powered 50 m Walk-In Conifer Elevator and Counterweight Winch
transport_and_power.description: Winch drum raised to 2.5 m (Cycle 78) so a full-height walk-in cabin meets the ground. Cabin framed from heavy conifer timbers (Cycle 84), hung on forged iron suspension brackets and braided cables (Cycle 85), balanced by about 200 kg of stone ballast in woven bags. Tested empty on a 50 m drop (Cycle 86). Powered by the windmill's sliding lantern-gear transmission from Cycle 103. Opens directly into the foyer. The old drum winch with 20 m grass cordage and a 40 kg boulder test dates to Cycle 44.
transport_and_power.image_prompt: A timber walk-in lift cabin built of heavy conifer logs hanging from forged iron brackets on thick braided rope over a 50-metre cliff drop, an iron-braced wooden winch drum above it inside a stone foyer.

transport_and_power.name: Vertical Cliff-Face 4-Sail Windmill
transport_and_power.description: Vertical wooden axle fixed to the cliff face with forged iron brackets and pegs (Cycle 91), four goat-hide sails on conifer timber frames added in Cycle 93. A sliding pine lantern-gear transmission shares power between the elevator winch, the hide bellows (via camshaft and lever) and the trip-hammer cam.
transport_and_power.image_prompt: A tall vertical wooden axle bolted to a sheer rock face carrying four stitched goat-hide sails on conifer frames, spinning in a gale beside a stone ledge.

transport_and_power.name: Sliding Lantern-Gear Transmission and Camshaft
transport_and_power.description: Carved pine lantern gear with locking pins, greased with animal fat, plus a fixed-ratio pine camshaft and wooden lever. A mechanical cone drive for variable speed was judged unbuildable and dropped (Cycle 96).
transport_and_power.image_prompt: A chunky carved pine lantern gear and a heavy cam lobe on a wooden shaft inside a stone alcove, fat-greased pegs and a long wooden lever.

interior_workshops_and_sectors.name: Original Ledge Shelter / Main Workshop Hall
interior_workshops_and_sectors.description: Mud-mortared dry-stack stone room with a door, drafts sealed with stone-dust-and-soil render (Cycle 37) and goat pelts pinned to interior walls for insulation (Cycle 43). Entry to the adit workings. Includes a heated mud-and-boulder bench (Cycle 25) and a tool and stone-cache corner.
interior_workshops_and_sectors.image_prompt: A snug rough-stone workshop interior lit by furnace glow, grey clay render on the walls, goat pelts pinned for insulation, a heated stone bench and tool racks.

interior_workshops_and_sectors.name: Lengthened Ceramic-and-Slate Cooking Stove
interior_workshops_and_sectors.description: Original circular furnace rebuilt with wet clay and flat stone into a long cooking stove with a sealed fire channel, tidy draft chimney at the far end and a broad slate top. Keeps the workshop at about 20C.
interior_workshops_and_sectors.image_prompt: A long clay-and-stone cooking stove capped with a broad slab of dark slate, goat meat searing on top, a tidy chimney at the far end.

interior_workshops_and_sectors.name: Central Circular Hearth Furnace
interior_workshops_and_sectors.description: Circular clay-and-cobble hearth furnace in the middle of the workshop floor, raised with the crew's help. Forged splint mail, spearheads, the trade token and the lock here (Cycles 55-62).
interior_workshops_and_sectors.image_prompt: A circular wet-clay and river-cobble hearth furnace at the centre of a stone workshop with an orange glowing heart, tongs and a basalt hammer beside it.

interior_workshops_and_sectors.name: Entrance-Wall Vented Stone Charcoal Kilns
interior_workshops_and_sectors.description: Row of charcoal furnaces set along the inside of the entrance wall, aligned with natural cracks for ventilation and connected to the old furnace vents. Overnight choked-furnace charcoal-making (Cycle 39) is a separate method.
interior_workshops_and_sectors.hallucination_reason: A sealed charcoal kiln was already present in Cycle 26 before any kiln was built (premature manifestation), and these built kilns were then forgotten in favour of outdoor clamps.
interior_workshops_and_sectors.image_prompt: A row of squat vented stone-and-clay charcoal furnaces along an interior stone wall, small iron-barred vent holes and sealed mud hatches.

interior_workshops_and_sectors.name: Quartz-Bauxite Crucible Furnace with Windmill-Driven Double Hide Bellows
interior_workshops_and_sectors.description: Ring of heat-resistant bauxite and quartz blocks at the base of the 85 cm cliff vent, with a layered chimney aligned to the shaft. Air throat widened (Cycle 97). Fed by a large double goat-hide bellows on pine-plank frames, sealed with animal fat and pine resin, nozzled into the throat and driven by the windmill camshaft (Cycle 98). Reached more than 1,300C white heat and produced the steel bloom of Cycle 102.
interior_workshops_and_sectors.image_prompt: A white-hot furnace of pale bauxite and quartz blocks with a tall layered chimney, a huge stitched goat-hide double bellows pumping into its throat, sparks and blinding glow.

interior_workshops_and_sectors.name: Large Double Goat-Hide Bellows
interior_workshops_and_sectors.description: Accordion bellows of flat planed pine boards wrapped in stitched goat pelt (bone awl and braided cordage), seams smeared with fat and pine resin; connected to the windmill camshaft. Replaced the small hand bellows of Cycle 26.
interior_workshops_and_sectors.image_prompt: A huge accordion bellows made from pine boards wrapped in stitched tan goat hide, seams glossy with fat and resin, a stone nozzle pointing into a furnace.

interior_workshops_and_sectors.name: Windmill-Driven Hardwood Trip-Hammer
interior_workshops_and_sectors.description: Heavy hardwood trunk bored for a fulcrum pin, lifted by wooden cam pegs on the windmill drive shaft and dropped on a massive basalt boulder anvil bed between two 2 m mortised conifer beams. Used in Cycle 116 to flatten lead-silver and copper into the rain basin.
interior_workshops_and_sectors.image_prompt: A huge hardwood trunk pivoted on a fulcrum between two mortised conifer beams, lifted by a pegged cam and about to drop on a black basalt boulder anvil.

interior_workshops_and_sectors.name: 5-Kilogram Forged Iron Anvil
interior_workshops_and_sectors.description: Forged from the iron wedge using crampon tongs and a basalt cobble: flat top, flared base.
interior_workshops_and_sectors.hallucination_reason: Equipment Degradation Hallucination: frequently downgraded in narrative text to a 'boulder anvil', 'stone bench' or 'basalt stone' because of context-window truncation. The iron anvil is canon.
interior_workshops_and_sectors.image_prompt: A small squat hand-forged iron anvil about five kilograms with a flat top and flared base, resting on a stout stump in firelight.

interior_workshops_and_sectors.name: Bark Quench Trough
interior_workshops_and_sectors.description: Bark trough of water used to temper hot-forged iron and splints. Sometimes filled with melted frost or bark water.
interior_workshops_and_sectors.image_prompt: A folded bark trough of dark water with steam rising as a glowing iron blade is plunged in.

interior_workshops_and_sectors.name: Sub-Zero Walk-In Permafrost Freezer
interior_workshops_and_sectors.description: Niche about 1 m deep cut into the quartz-veined rear wall of the original shelter; the rock bleeds sub-zero chill and keeps meat (9 kg stored first). A planned larger freezer on the outer front wall and a connecting fridge are only on the settlement map.
interior_workshops_and_sectors.image_prompt: A deep dark niche cut in a quartz-veined rock wall with frost on its sides and wrapped cuts of goat meat stacked inside, a stacked-slab door beside it.

interior_workshops_and_sectors.name: Right-Flank Mining and Residential Corridor
interior_workshops_and_sectors.description: Corridor driven into the rock from the workshop with quartz and hematite bands deliberately left as wall decoration (Cycle 72). Contains a 2 m deep sleeping alcove (Cycle 80) with a wooden door and moss pallets, and the copper and lead-silver vein face reached at its end (Cycle 87). Total excavated length is not recorded in the chronicle; the earlier 22.5 m figure is unverified.
interior_workshops_and_sectors.image_prompt: A freshly cut rock corridor with white quartz and rust-red iron bands left bare as decoration, a pickaxe and bags of rubble on the floor, a sleeping alcove with moss pallets.

interior_workshops_and_sectors.name: Four Stone-and-Hide Guest Bunks
interior_workshops_and_sectors.description: Four raised stone platforms levelled with gravel and layered with conifer branches, grass and scrap hide. Later replaced in daily use by moss pallets.
interior_workshops_and_sectors.image_prompt: Four raised rough-stone bunks padded with conifer boughs and goat hides in a row inside a warm stone room.

interior_workshops_and_sectors.name: Stone Water Basin
interior_workshops_and_sectors.description: Natural stone basin fed by melting frost trickling off the cliff above; later also used for melting ice and boiling water.
interior_workshops_and_sectors.image_prompt: A natural stone basin collecting a slow clear trickle of meltwater under a frosty cliff face.

records_and_libraries.name: Abacus Wall, Slate Library and Peg-Board Lookup Board
records_and_libraries.description: Wall-grid of grooves with sliding wooden pegs tracks resource stock (Cycle 48). Numbered slate blueprint library in a corner cache (Cycle 57). 100 forged flat-topped iron ID pegs (Cycle 74). Lookup tables on slate: crew and action IDs (Cycles 75-76), materials (Cycle 76), components (Cycle 82), master index (Cycle 84). The planned wooden cabinet with ten-person rows and ten-tablet ring binder is NOT built for lack of lumber.
records_and_libraries.image_prompt: A rough rock wall carved with a grid of grooves and sliding wooden pegs beside stacks of numbered dark slate tablets and a pouch of small flat-topped iron pegs.

records_and_libraries.name: Stone Task List Slab
records_and_libraries.description: Square slab carved into the wall listing sleep, eat, hunt, train and survival routines. Entry '0 Days Food' was carved in Cycle 30 then crossed out in Cycle 31.
records_and_libraries.image_prompt: A square slab chiselled into a rock wall with rows of crude symbols and a short list of daily tasks.

records_and_libraries.name: Master Settlement Map Slab and Slate Table
records_and_libraries.description: Wide slate slab carved with Industry, Armoury, Sustenance and Great Hall districts plus runic wayfinding marks (Cycle 49). Later updated in charcoal on a slate table (see settlement_plan_map).
records_and_libraries.image_prompt: A wide dark slate table scratched with charcoal lines showing halls, corridors and rooms of a mountain settlement, small runic arrows in the margins.

records_and_libraries.name: Workshop Rules Slab
records_and_libraries.description: Three engraved rules: restock used charcoal by firing more; restock used forging resources; workshop tools remain the property of the workshop. Stands by the door.
records_and_libraries.image_prompt: A flat slate slab carved with three short lines of rules, propped beside a stone doorway.

records_and_libraries.name: Daily Plans Slate and Morning Meeting Notes
records_and_libraries.description: Wipeable slate tile titled 'Daily Plans' with charcoal task assignments, refreshed at the regular morning meeting. Meeting notes also recorded on slate (Cycle 107). Wishlist slates by Roseblossom (poncho) and Helrune (insulated leg wraps) are filed in the library (Cycle 58).
records_and_libraries.image_prompt: A dark slate tile with the words DAILY PLANS scratched across the top and charcoal checklists beneath, smudged by hands, on a stone table.

excavation_state.summary: Work is hand-mined with picks along the right-flank corridor and the rear adit. Roughing out of the Grand Banquet Hall and Grand Workshop ceilings began in Cycle 104; an interior tunnel beneath the frozen pool was started in Cycles 117 and 119-120. No finished hall or workshop dome exists yet.
excavation_state.image_prompt: A cross-section of a mountain tunnel with a dwarf and elf swinging pickaxes at a rock face striped with white quartz and rust-red hematite, rubble bags and a lantern.

inventory_pointers.latest_stock_notes: Hematite: 60 kg charged to the furnace on Cycle 101; fresh veins exposed in the adit. Copper matte and lead-silver bullion: consumed forging the rain basin (Cycle 116). Charcoal: second clamp smouldering. Food: young goat kid roasted Cycle 122; freezer niche meat stock not re-counted. Water: basin rainwater plus meltwater.

planned_sectors.name: Mountain Entry Room (Armour and Ice-Boot Room)
planned_sectors.description: Stout room at the mountain entrance for removing heavy armour and muddy ice crampons, followed by a short corridor to the banquet hall.
planned_sectors.image_prompt: A stout stone entry chamber with wall pegs for armour and crampons, a bench and muddy boot marks, a short corridor beyond.

planned_sectors.name: Grand Banquet Hall (200 seats)
planned_sectors.description: Hall seating 200 with long tables and wide walking lanes; buffet along the left side serving from an adjoining kitchen with open walkways on both sides; corridors to the residential wing (right) and the kitchen and far-end corridor to the central intersection.
planned_sectors.image_prompt: A vast carved-stone dwarven banquet hall with long rows of rough tables for two hundred, a buffet counter on the left, glowing ore veins in the walls and iron lamps.

planned_sectors.name: Kitchen for Four Cooks with Freezer and Fridge
planned_sectors.description: Wide prep benches, heavy stoves and dry pantry storage; a walk-in freezer on the frozen outer front wall linked to a walk-in fridge that opens into the kitchen.
planned_sectors.image_prompt: A stone kitchen with four wide prep benches, heavy clay stoves and shelved pantry, a frost-rimed rock door leading to a cold store.

planned_sectors.name: Sleeping Quarters Corridor
planned_sectors.description: 20 m corridor bending 90 degrees from the banquet hall's right side with three evenly spaced doorways on its right into rooms with multiple beds, storage, a door and rough-hewn walls.
planned_sectors.image_prompt: A bending rock corridor with three timber doors on one side, each opening to a rough-hewn bedroom with bunks and storage niches.

planned_sectors.name: Communal Washhouse and Latrines
planned_sectors.description: Large bathroom on the corridor's left with multiple stone toilets and washbasins, doors to the corridor and directly to the banquet hall, vent draft to avoid stale air.
planned_sectors.image_prompt: A stone washhouse with a row of carved stone basins and toilet stalls and a gentle draft vent in the ceiling.

planned_sectors.name: Far-End Corridor and Central Intersection
planned_sectors.description: 20 m corridor from the end of the banquet hall to a wide central intersection with load-bearing pillars; left branch to the kitchen, right to the sleeping corridor.
planned_sectors.image_prompt: A wide stone intersection with thick carved pillars where four corridors meet, torchlight and iron-banded doors.

planned_sectors.name: Grand Workshop (50 m Domed Chamber)
planned_sectors.description: Vast 50 m diameter domed chamber off the intersection with thick wooden support arches, arch locking stones holding the dome, and vents redirecting rising heat to the settlement.
planned_sectors.image_prompt: A huge domed forge-hall carved in a mountain, thick timber arches and wedge keystones locking the stone dome, forges and anvils glowing below, heat vents above.

planned_sectors.name: Armoury and Warehouse (Stock Manifest)
planned_sectors.description: Stocked with ingots, steel axes, arrow tips, butchering knives, daggers, steel claws, iron cams and axles, steel blacksmith hammers, swords, full-body steel armour, iron rail-cart tracks and clay-lined personal heater boxes. Stock counts are quotas only; none yet made.
planned_sectors.image_prompt: A mountain armoury with racks of steel swords, axes and full plate suits, stacked iron ingots and rail-cart tracks, stone shelves under lantern light.

mechanical engineering (winch, windmill, cam, trip-hammer, bellows)
slate blueprint drafting and record keeping

fire clay crucibles and blister steel
excavate the Grand Banquet Hall and Grand Workshop
build a blast furnace for cast iron

characters.name: Helrune

notable_events: Careful clean skinning of the goat kid (Cycle 97, 121-122).

Asked for rain catch basins at the midday council (Cycle 115).
Summit water scouting cancelled for a storm (Cycle 81).

processes_and_recipes.name: Bloomery Steel Smelt (Verified Method, Cycles 98-103)
processes_and_recipes.summary: Forced-draft bloomery smelt in the quartz-bauxite furnace producing a carbon-rich steel bloom that is hammered into tool heads. This is the method that actually worked and should be reused until a better one exists.
inputs: clean charcoal from a turf clamp
windmill-driven large hide bellows and camshaft
pine leaf-spring handle and iron wedge
steps: Cut and stack conifer softwood and scrub boughs around a central flue; bury under turf, dirt and shale; ignite and smother-smoulder into clean light charcoal (clamp, Cycles 98 and 101).
Widen the furnace air throat and fit the large sealed goat-hide double bellows (fat and pine resin on seams) to a stone nozzle, connected to the windmill camshaft via a wooden lever (Cycle 98).
Smash hematite to pebble-sized pieces and layer it in the furnace under charcoal (60 kg charge, Cycle 101).
Engage the transmission so the windmill pumps the bellows; hold white heat (over 1,300C) for hours.
Break open the furnace base and drag the spitting bloom out with greenwood tongs; its outer crust has absorbed carbon and is steel (Cycle 102).
Reheat and hammer on the anvil, driving out slag and folding or drawing the bloom; split off a billet and shape a tapered head.
Punch the eye, quench the edge, then fit to a leaf-spring pine handle with an iron wedge through the crown (Cycle 103).
processes_and_recipes.limits: Yield was one tool head per smelt effort because of reheating labour and bellows size. The trip-hammer (built Cycle 104) is expected to speed forging.
processes_and_recipes.image_prompt: A roaring white-hot furnace of pale blocks with a stitched hide bellows pumping, a dwarf dragging a glowing steel bloom out with long green-wood tongs, sparks everywhere.

processes_and_recipes.name: Blister Steel in Clay Crucibles (Proposed Method, Cycle 119)
processes_and_recipes.summary: Seal wrought iron in tight clay crucibles packed with crushed charcoal and bake under forced air for hours until the iron absorbs carbon, then hammer and fold. Entangled's Cycle 119 explanation; it contradicts the earlier bloom-based method only in framing, not in physical result.
inputs: clay-quartz crucibles with lids (drying since Cycle 122)
steps: Pack wrought iron bars and crushed charcoal into sealed crucibles.
Bake in the windmill-blown furnace for hours.
Cool, hammer and fold the blistered metal.
processes_and_recipes.image_prompt: A lidded clay crucible packed with black charcoal and iron bars glowing inside a white-hot furnace.

processes_and_recipes.name: Charcoal Clamp (Turf-and-Dirt Burn)
processes_and_recipes.summary: Stack softwood and scrub around a flue, cover with turf and dirt, light from the core and leave to smoulder.
steps: Stack timber tight around a central flue.
Blanket with turf, soil and crushed shale.
Drop embers down the flue and seal the top.
Wait; open when cool for brittle, light charcoal.

key_events_timeline.event: Entangled arrives on the southern cliffs and builds a corbelled stone bunker around an old windbreak with a wired horn.
First fire from flint, first spear; kills a predatory lizard and cures its hide.
Night scouting north finds a timber road, two dead trolls and the sea-cave drift mine.
Attempt to dig the cave fails; dwarf realises iron tools are essential.
Kills first goat; pelt, sinew and meat acquired.
Bone needle made.
Shale slab windbreak door; runic quartz pickaxe made and tested; ledger note.
Stone ledger inventory and periscope sketch; quartz mirror grinding fails.
Hematite pocket found in the cave wall.
Decision to leave the cold coast for the Lone Mountain.
Floodplain crossing; four raptor claws; limonite chunks; crampons first appear.
Three-clawed glove crafted at the gravel bar camp.
Climbs the zigzag gully and finds the bloomery ledge camp: Malmskor's birthplace.
Carves a path down the gully; plank door hung; clay render fails; hyrax killed.
Furnace, chimney and vents built; heated bench; hide vest.
5 kg iron anvil forged; 25 kg ore hauled by sled; food at zero.
Ancestral rune ritual fails; no magic.
Hot-forged sword and pick; stone-dust render; seamless plank door installed.
Iron brackets and axe forged; first winch tested with a 40 kg boulder; timber hauled.
Iron claws replace raptor claws; four guest beds built.
Permafrost walk-in freezer niche cut; 9 kg meat stored.
Masked elf ambush: Entangled wounded in shoulder and thigh; attacker flees east; abacus wall built.
Wound care; master settlement map slab; furnace converted into cooking stove.
Dede, Helrune and Roseblossom climb the winch rope and join Entangled.
Central hearth and charcoal furnaces begun; workshop rules carved; raw copper supplied.
Splint mail chest guard, three iron spears, trade token, boulder barricade.
Slate library and filing system begun.
Tumbler lock forged; raw-hide curing lesson.
Knuckle spike gauntlet and brigandine vest made; lock installed.
Settlement map updated with entry room, corridor and 200-seat banquet hall.
Ore veins marked as decoration; quartz-bauxite furnace and layered chimney built.
Second gauntlet finished; 100 iron ID pegs forged.
Winch raised to 2.5 m; 60 kg of hematite hauled out.
Settlement named Malmskor (Iron Ledge); elevator cabin hung on brackets.
First 50 m elevator drop test passes; hand-hauling too hard.
Copper and lead-silver vein found; silver beads seen.
450 g lead-silver bullion and 650 g copper matte smelted; ice pool found 40 m east.
Pipeline fails to the cold; windmill axle bolted to the cliff.
Four hide sails fitted; windmill spins.
Large sealed hide bellows connected to windmill camshaft; charcoal clamp lit.
Clamp opened; 60 kg hematite charged; windmill-blown smelt begins.
Steel bloom pulled from the furnace.
Steel pickaxe fitted; windmill drives elevator winch and bellows through gears.
Windmill trip-hammer built and tested.
Slanted-roof foyer built.
Foyer rebuilt to enclose the winch and elevator entry.
Defence tower foundation ring laid.
Foyer sealed with mortar; crossbow nut, sear and bracket forged.
Magic-awakening dream has no real effect.
Rain basin forged under the trip-hammer; crossbow found to lack a prod.
Steel-making method reviewed; blister-steel crucible process proposed.
Tower interior rendered; dome postponed; crew hunts goat kid and gathers softwood.
Second charcoal clamp lit; clay crucibles moulded.
Ledger inspection wrongly records built fixtures as unbuilt.
Ledger corrected; lock, elevator and freezer confirmed; catfolk hunter seeking Ryu arrives.

continuity_flags.summary: Wired wooden horn and microphone present in the original windbreak.
continuity_flags.guidance: Treat as pre-existing curiosity; do not build on it unless a later cycle explains it.

continuity_flags.summary: Pre-excavated drift mine, woven fish trap and frozen clay mound found in the sea cave.
Scrap-iron crampons appear without being crafted.
continuity_flags.guidance: Keep as canon equipment; list in inventory.

continuity_flags.summary: Established bloomery camp with bauxite-ironstone windbreaks found on the ledge.
continuity_flags.guidance: Canon: the ledge camp predates Entangled; do not make it the player's own handiwork.

continuity_flags.summary: A sealed kiln with charcoal and a hide bellows appear in Cycle 26 before being built.
continuity_flags.guidance: Assume a small clay kiln and a crude bellows exist; real kilns are W3 (Cycle 54).

continuity_flags.summary: The 5 kg iron anvil is repeatedly described as a boulder, stone bench or basalt.
continuity_flags.guidance: Iron anvil is canon; the trip-hammer anvil bed is a separate basalt boulder.

continuity_flags.summary: A 20 m grass cord is used to winch over and down a 50 m cliff.
continuity_flags.guidance: Cables and rope later described as thick braided cables; assume more cordage was made.

continuity_flags.summary: Roseblossom specified as a male halfling in prompts but written as female from Cycle 58.
continuity_flags.guidance: Current usage is female; keep until confirmed otherwise.

continuity_flags.summary: Warning sign was to be at the start of the path below but is propped at the ledge.
Copper wire rivets and 'melted copper ore' appear before wire drawing or the copper vein discovery.
continuity_flags.guidance: Allowed from the single raw copper lump; no wire-drawing yet.

continuity_flags.summary: Dede says there is no copper though a lump was supplied; and the 'C3' label clashed with Helrune's ID.
continuity_flags.guidance: Copper exists in small quantity; C3 is Helrune only.

continuity_flags.summary: Four iron-and-charcoal heat boxes requested; only two iron boxes forged in Cycle 92, four clay-quartz boxes moulded in Cycles 93-94.
Open turf clamps used for charcoal despite the W3 indoor charcoal kilns.
continuity_flags.guidance: Both exist; clamps are used for bulk steel-grade charcoal.

continuity_flags.summary: Steel was made by a windmill-blown bloomery smelt (Cycles 101-102), yet in Cycle 119 Entangled says steel needs blister work in crucibles.
continuity_flags.guidance: Both methods are recorded: bloomery steel is the verified one; blister steel is the proposed second method (see processes_and_recipes).

continuity_flags.summary: Four steel pickaxes ordered; only one steel head made. Three more are outstanding.
Cycle 123 wrongly logged the elevator, lock and freezer as unbuilt; corrected in Cycle 124.
continuity_flags.guidance: These fixtures are built and operational.

continuity_flags.summary: The crossbow was said to be built but had no prod; the tower dome is also unbuilt.
continuity_flags.guidance: Status stays Partially Built / Under Construction.

continuity_flags.summary: The earlier database quoted a 22.5 m corridor depth that the chronicle does not support.
continuity_flags.guidance: Use incremental figures: 2 m alcove, +1.5 m at the vein face.

continuity_flags.summary: Prompt facility codes (F3-F10, W5-W7) are used without definitions.

Fire clay crucibles and run a blister-steel batch when the second charcoal clamp is ready.

Continue excavating the Grand Banquet Hall and Grand Workshop and the tunnel beneath the frozen pool.

Build a blast furnace to enable cast iron gears, wire dies, rolling mills and pipes.
